messages.text: (The customer sent this photo without a message.)

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist, Sarah passed this over to me.

I opened your screenshot. It shows the station reporting temperature 9999.0 °C and humidity 9999.0 %, wind average 0.0 m/s, while pressure reads a normal 1013.8 hPa. Those 9999 values are not real readings, they are the "no valid data" placeholder the app shows when the temperature/humidity sensor is not answering. Pressure being fine tells me the board and the link to the app are alive, so this is most likely the T/H sensor element or its connection, not the whole station.

One check first, so I know if it is a glitch or a hard fault:

1. Power cycle the station: take it down, remove the batteries (or unplug power) for 60 seconds, put them back and let it sit outside for 15 to 20 minutes.
2. Then open the app and tell me what temperature and humidity show.

While it is in your hands, also tell me: roughly when did the 9999 readings start, and had anything happened just before (heavy rain, cleaning, a battery change)?

Thanks, that helps: a few days of 9999 means it is not a one-off glitch.

Next step, the power cycle:

1. Bring the station down and remove the batteries (or unplug it) for a full 60 seconds.
2. Put the power back, remount it and leave it 15 to 20 minutes.
3. Open the app and tell me what temperature and humidity show then.

Two things to check while you are in the app, so I do not have you climbing twice:

- Devices tab, open the station: does it show a firmware version and is an update offered?
- Does it say the station is online with a recent "last seen" time?
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Searched the web · SKY-100 weather station 9999 temperature humidity reading
Searched the web · SKY-100 DePIN weather station low battery sensor not reporti

Thanks, that screenshot tells me a lot. Reading it back: Sky-Purdey, SKY-100, Status Online, last observation 2026-10-29 20:15, online 11 hours, signal Fair, firmware 25.02266, and battery at 22%.

So the station is talking to the network fine. The one thing that stands out is the battery at 22%. The S.100 is a battery powered unit, and when the pack gets low the sensor block is the first thing that stops returning valid samples, which is exactly what the 9999 placeholders mean. A few days of 9999 lines up with a pack that has been slowly draining.

Next step, before anything else:

1. Charge the station to 100% (leave it on the charger, it can take several hours).
2. Once it is full, power cycle it: off for 60 seconds, then back on.
3. Leave it 20 minutes, then open the app and tell me what temperature and humidity show, plus the battery percentage.

If it is on solar or sitting somewhere shaded, tell me where it is mounted too. A panel in shade this time of year will not keep up, and that alone can explain the drift down to 22%.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

I opened it. The D. list shows Sky-Purdey online (green dot), last observation 20:15 today, and the orange battery icon with the lightning bolt in the corner, so the station is on charge right now. Good, that is exactly the step I wanted.

Let it run up to 100%. Then:

1. Power it off for 60 seconds and back on.
2. Give it 20 minutes outside.
3. Send me the Dashboard screen again, so I can see whether temperature and humidity come back with real numbers or still show 9999.

If it still reads 9999 on a full battery, that points at the sensor head itself rather than power, and I will take it from there.
I get back to you tomorrow

Sounds good, Pascal. Charge it to 100%, power cycle it, then send me the Dashboard screen and we pick up right there.

If it still shows 9999 after a full charge, mention it when you write back and we go straight to the sensor head checks. Talk tomorrow.
